title: Winning it back
situation: On your paper account, a GBP/USD trade just hit your [[stop-loss|stop loss]] for a loss of 40 USD. It was a planned trade with a planned stop. You feel angry and want to win the money back before the session ends.
question: What do you do next?

responses.text: Open a new trade straight away in the opposite direction.
responses.explanation: This trade is driven by wanting to undo the loss, not by a setup in your plan.

responses.text: Take the next trade at double the size, so one win covers the loss.
responses.explanation: Raising size to recover a loss adds risk at the moment your judgement is under the most pressure. A second loss would be twice as big.

responses.text: Step away for a set time, then log the trade and check whether you followed your plan.
responses.explanation: A pause breaks the link between the loss and the next decision. If you followed your plan, the loss was a cost you already accepted.

responses.text: Stay at the screen and watch closely for the next setup.
responses.explanation: Watching is not trading, but staying glued to the chart while upset makes a rushed entry more likely.

takeaway: A planned loss is part of trading. The next trade should come from your plan, not from wanting to get even.
